introduction: Today we celebrate the Most Holy Trinity: one God, Father, Son and Holy Spirit. Moses tells the people that no nation ever had a God so close to them. Paul says that the Spirit makes us children of God who can call him Abba, Father. Jesus sends his disciples to baptize in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit. Let us worship the God who has drawn us into his own life.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, we were baptized in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit. Let us pray to the Father, through the Son, in the Spirit.
intentions: For the Church: that she may make disciples of all nations and baptize them in the name of the Holy Trinity. Let us pray to the Lord.
For families: that they may reflect the love of the Trinity in their unity, respect and care for one another. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who feel like orphans, alone or unloved: that the Spirit may assure them that they are children of God. Let us pray to the Lord.
For all who doubt or search for God: that they may discover a God who is near and who speaks to them. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that each Sign of the Cross we make may be an act of faith and love. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: God our Father, you sent your Son and your Spirit to make us your children. Keep us faithful to our Baptism and bring us at last to share your life for ever. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Abba, Father
reflection.body:
The Trinity can sound like a puzzle for theologians. Yet today's readings speak of it in a very personal way: a God who comes close.

Moses asks the people to look back over all history: "Did a people ever hear the voice of God speaking out of the middle of the fire, as you have heard, and live?" Israel's God is not a distant force. He chose a people and acted for them. "Know therefore today, and take it to heart, that the LORD himself is God in heaven above and on the earth beneath. There is no one else."

Paul tells us how close this God has come. Through the Spirit we are not slaves but children: "you received the Spirit of adoption," by whom we cry, Abba, Father And "The Spirit himself testifies with our spirit that we are children of God." The Father, the Son and the Spirit are not three facts about God; they are the way God has loved us and drawn us in.

In the Gospel, the risen Jesus sends his disciples to all nations, "baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit." Some of them still doubt, Matthew tells us, but Jesus sends them anyway, with a promise: "Behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the age."

We were baptized into that name. Every time we make the Sign of the Cross, we remember who we belong to. This week, make it slowly and deliberately each morning, and pray to each of the three Persons in turn: thank the Father, follow the Son, and ask the Spirit to guide you.
